status: revised outcome-blind species mapping after v1 prefix-count failure, still before any numeric height value is opened

history.v1_result: FAIL: all raw GPS ID strings partitioned as D=11 and H=8, not the published 9 and 8 tracked individuals

source_evidence.paper_statement: We tracked nine H. armiger individuals and eight H. pratti individuals.

mapping_algorithm: Using presence-qualified rows only, count ID x nocturnal-session rows without parsing numeric height.
Apply the already-frozen >=50-fixes-per-session threshold; no new threshold is introduced for mapping.
Define source-effective tracked IDs as IDs with at least one >=50-fix session.
Proceed only if source-effective IDs total exactly 17 and split into exactly two leading-prefix groups with counts 9 and 8.
Map the 9-ID prefix to Hipposideros armiger and the 8-ID prefix to Hipposideros pratti, matching the paper's explicit tracked counts.
Raw IDs with zero >=50-fix sessions are retained in provenance as structurally unusable and cannot enter the later repeat-individual validation gate anyway.
If any of these exact conditions fail, declare MAPPING_UNRESOLVED and do not open numeric height.
why_not_outcome_guided: The >=50 session threshold was frozen before raw access as the primary structural eligibility rule.
Only ID strings, timestamps, coordinates needed for row qualification, and height presence/nonblank status are used; height magnitude is never parsed.
The paper's 9/8 species counts are public source metadata and predate this analysis.
No vertical statistic has been opened in the Hipposideros family.
claim_boundary: This mapping identifies species only for source-effective IDs under the pre-existing structural threshold.
D21 and D22 remain in raw-file provenance but are not used to manufacture the 9/8 split; they fail the pre-frozen full-session threshold.
The subsequent primary validation still requires >=2 qualifying nights plus >=50 common-support target events.
